item.title: Sengan-en Garden — Guide
item.description: Sengan-en, on the shore of Kinko Bay just north of Kagoshima city, is one of Japan’s finest traditional gardens and a former villa of the powerful Shimazu clan, who ruled the region for nearly 700 years. Laid out in the seventeenth century, its genius lies in its ‘borrowed scenery’ (shakkei): the garden is designed so that the smoking cone of Sakurajima volcano across the bay becomes its centrepiece ‘mountain’, with the sea as its ‘pond’, creating a breathtaking, grand-scale landscape.

item.title: Sengan-en Winter Illumination — Guide
item.description: Each winter (typically around December into January), the magnificent Sengan-en garden — the former villa of the Shimazu lords on Kinko Bay — hosts a beautiful evening illumination, transforming the historic landscape garden into a magical nighttime spectacle. As dusk falls, the garden’s ponds, streams, trees, stone lanterns and elegant buildings are lit up with warm lights and colourful displays, their reflections shimmering in the still water. The historic Shimazu residence and the grounds take on a romantic, dreamlike glow, and seasonal decorations and light installations add to the festive winter atmosphere.
